1 Peter 1:6-9 (KJV) “6 Wherein ye greatly rejoice, though now for a season, if need be, ye are in heaviness through manifold temptations:”

-Peter started his letter by encouraging the brethren, reminding us of who we are in Christ and all that God has done for us through salvation, how He preserves us by His power while we’re on earth and how the kingdom of heaven is being reserved for us as our inheritance, in all these things we should greatly rejoice. However we all know that once we give our life to Christ it’s not all sunshine and lollipops, or at least we should. We need to realize we are in a battle, a spiritual battle that will wage on until Christ comes and sets things straight. Just as the brethren were facing many trials and struggles during this time so too are we. It’s easy to get “battle fatigue” during these times of various trials and afflictions that come upon us which allows heaviness (sadness, sorrow, grief, or maybe even anger, resentment, fear, anxiety) to take its toll. The battles we face aren’t just on the outside but on the inside. We now have two natures that are warring against each other, the sin nature that won’t be completely done away with until our redemption is complete when we are finally in the presence of God and the Holy Spirit who now lives within us who desires to conform us into the image of Christ. The trials that the Lord allows us to go through are for a purpose, a reason, to do a work within us, it’s a part of the sanctification process where He is purifying us.

“7 That the trial of your faith, being much more precious than of gold that perisheth, though it be tried with fire, might be found unto praise and honour and glory at the appearing of Jesus Christ: 8 Whom having not seen, ye love; in whom, though now ye see him not, yet believing, ye rejoice with joy unspeakable and full of glory: 9 Receiving the end of your faith, even the salvation of your souls.”

-Our faith in Jesus Christ is the most precious thing that we possess, greater than anything this world has to offer because our faith is what produces salvation in us and gives us eternal life with the Lord. These trials of our faith are designed to refine us. A beautiful picture of this is how the goldsmith would purify gold in ancient times. Before refinement the gold had a bunch of impurities that had to be removed and the only way to do that was through fire. The goldsmith would put the gold in a crucible and slowly heat up the gold which caused the dross, or impurities, to rise to the top so that he could easily scoop them out. He would then heat it up even higher and continue to scoop out the dross until it was all gone. This was a very tedious process and it relied on an expert craftsman to perform because if the fire got too hot too quickly it could scorch the gold and ruin it. The goldsmith was present during this entire time and paid close attention to the gold until the process was complete and the end result was pure gold. How did he know when the process was complete? He could look into the gold and see his own reflection. This is how we should look at our trials. We have impurities, dross, in our lives because of sin. The Lord desires to purify His people and one way He does this is through trials. When we are in the fire of a trial and all that yuckiness is coming out of us and the heat seems at times too much to bear, we have to remember that’s it’s during these times that the Lord is right there with us, watching over us, paying close attention not only to us but the heat of the flame making sure that it doesn’t scorch and ruin us (even though we might feel like it is) until the process is complete and He can see His own reflection in us. It’s also during these times of trials that our faith grows and matures and we see His faithfulness in return. We have to cling to the promise that is given to us in Romans 8:28, “And we know that all things work together for good to them that love God, to them who are the called according to his purpose.” The end result of this is the salvation of our souls, that our faith may be found to the the praise and honor and glory at the appearing of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ who died so that we may live, who resurrected from the dead conquering sin and death so that we may have eternal life and have victory over them. We love Him, even though we’ve not yet laid eyes on Him, we know that He is real, we trust in what He did for us, and we wait in earnest expectation of that day when we shall see Him face to face. This is what keeps us going, this is what helps us through our dark times because we realize this life is a vapor and when it’s over we will finally know and understand and experience what true life is all about for we shall obtain the inheritance that’s awaiting us in eternity. This is how we can have joy unspeakable on this earth with all the hardships and the pain because we have glory waiting on us!
